title: Exclusive Interview with CLO Founder Jaden: Revealing the Stories Behind CLO and MD, a Must-Learn for Fashion Designers!
description:
Jaden Oh, founder of CLO Virtual Fashion, appeared on the program "The Globalist" to reveal the technological power behind movie character costumes! Designers use two software programs, CLO and Marvelous Designer, to transform creativity into shining stars in the fashion, film, and gaming industries. With unprecedented efficiency and an eco-friendly approach, creativity freely blossoms in the digital world. Another software under CLO, Jinny, makes design dreams within reach, breaking down professional barriers so that ordinary people who aspire to design but have never ventured into it can easily create the clothing they envision.

The vision of CLO Virtual Fashion is also gradually being realized through CLO-SET, an integrated platform that consolidates design assets, enables information sharing, and supports metaverse marketing, drawing a new blueprint for the future of the fashion industry!

chunks.title: Exclusive Interview with CLO Founder Jaden: Revealing the Stories Behind CLO and MD, a Must-Learn for Fashion Designers!
chunks.content: # Exclusive Interview with CLO Founder Jaden Oh: The Stories Behind CLO and MD for Fashion Designers This document covers key insights from Jaden Oh, founder of CLO Virtual Fashion and creator of Marvelous Designer, focusing on virtual garment technology, its applications in fashion and filmmaking, sustainability impacts, and future directions including the new software Genie. --- ## Introduction to CLO Virtual Fashion and Marvelous Designer This section explains CLO Virtual Fashion's core technology, Marvelous Designer (MD), and its role in virtual garment creation for fashion and film industries. Jaden Oh is the founder of CLO Virtual Fashion, a company pioneering software that virtualizes garments for fashion designers and enthusiasts globally. The flagship product, Marvelous Designer, offers a unique approach to digital clothing design based on computer simulation rather than traditional sculpting. This simulation mimics real-world garment construction by assembling multiple 2D fabric patterns into 3D garments. Unlike earlier tools that sculpted wrinkles and folds piece by piece—a time-consuming and expert-driven process—Marvelous Designer uses physics-based cloth simulation, allowing fast, accurate, and realistic draping of garments. This technology enables designers to visualize garments digitally before physical production, drastically reducing time and resource waste. --- ## Marvelous Designer’s Impact on the Film Industry This section details how Marvelous Designer revolutionized costume design in filmmaking with accurate, efficient garment visualization. Marvelous Designer has been widely adopted by the film industry for creating digital costumes in major productions such as *Black Panther*, *Avatar*, and *Guardians of the Galaxy*. The software supports pre-visualization processes, allowing costume designers to create 3D versions of garments to visualize how costumes look on characters before physical fabrication or filming. This is especially important in scenes involving CGI, fantasy storytelling, or dangerous stunts where real costumes may be impractical. The software’s simulation technology replaced the laborious sculpting of digital garments, providing realistic folds, wrinkles, and movement, thus enhancing the visual effects quality and efficiency. --- ## Use of CLO Software in Fashion Industry and Sustainability Benefits This section explores how CLO software supports fashion brands like H&M and Louis Vuitton by enabling 3D sample creation, reducing fabric waste, and promoting sustainability. Fashion brands utilize CLO’s software to replace multiple physical samples with 3D digital prototypes. This shift significantly reduces fabric consumption and waste, contributing positively to environmental sustainability. High-end brands like Louis Vuitton require extremely high-quality 3D samples that faithfully replicate real garments, including detailed components such as buttons, zippers, stitches, and trims. CLO’s software offers over 800 functions to refine these details in real-time, enabling designers to work as precisely as with physical garments. Additionally, the fashion industry leverages 3D content for communication with suppliers, virtual fashion shows, virtual showrooms, and virtual try-ons, further reducing carbon emissions by minimizing physical shipments and travel. --- ## Origins and Development of CLO and Marvelous Designer This section covers Jaden Oh’s background, the origins of CLO, and the evolution of Marvelous Designer from a niche tool for virtual cosplay to a mainstream software for fashion and film professionals.

chunks.content: CLO’s software offers over 800 functions to refine these details in real-time, enabling designers to work as precisely as with physical garments. Additionally, the fashion industry leverages 3D content for communication with suppliers, virtual fashion shows, virtual showrooms, and virtual try-ons, further reducing carbon emissions by minimizing physical shipments and travel. --- ## Origins and Development of CLO and Marvelous Designer This section covers Jaden Oh’s background, the origins of CLO, and the evolution of Marvelous Designer from a niche tool for virtual cosplay to a mainstream software for fashion and film professionals. Jaden Oh, a computer scientist with a family background in clothing retail, began research on real-time cloth simulation over 20 years ago. His master's thesis included developing applications for online clothing simulation, which later evolved into Marvelous Designer. Initially, the software attracted a community of virtual cosplay enthusiasts who created digital costumes and tutorials, helping spread international recognition. This community-driven growth led to adoption by major VFX studios such as Weta Digital. The transition from sculpting-based tools to simulation-based software marked a paradigm shift, enabling rapid and realistic garment modeling. --- ## Technical Features and Challenges in Achieving Realism This section outlines the technical complexity behind CLO’s cloth simulation and the ongoing challenges in achieving lifelike garment quality. The software models garments as assemblies of 2D patterns sewn together, simulating fabric behavior through physics-based algorithms. Achieving the precise wrinkle formation, drape, and interaction requires extensive computation and advanced simulation techniques. Over a decade of development has resulted in more than 800 features supporting detailed components like buttons, zippers, stitches, and accessory trims. Despite these advances, challenges remain in balancing realism with usability and computational efficiency. --- ## Introduction of Genie: Democratizing 3D Garment Creation This section introduces Genie, CLO’s new software designed for non-experts to create 3D garments without pattern-making knowledge. While Marvelous Designer and CLO cater to professionals with expertise in garment patterns, Genie targets casual users and beginners by simplifying the garment design process. Genie allows users to create 3D clothing more easily, although some knowledge is still needed to produce real-life garments. The software carries full pattern and sewing information enabling 3D garments to be manufactured physically. This bridges the gap between digital design and real-world production. --- ## Personal Motivation and Vision Behind CLO This section shares Jaden Oh’s personal story and motivation for creating accessible garment design tools. Jaden’s motivation includes a personal story about his son attempting to create a garment using their software but failing due to complex patterns. This inspired the development of Genie to empower non-professionals, including children, to design and produce real garments. He emphasizes that his goal is to create software that his children and others can use to realize their creative ideas in fashion. --- ## Future Vision: CLOSET Platform and Industry Transformation This section discusses CLO’s future direction with the CLOSET platform aimed at revolutionizing the entire fashion lifecycle.

Jaden Oh is the founder of CLO Virtual Fashion, a company pioneering software that virtualizes garments for fashion designers and enthusiasts globally. The flagship product, Marvelous Designer, offers a unique approach to digital clothing design based on computer simulation rather than traditional sculpting. This simulation mimics real-world garment construction by assembling multiple 2D fabric patterns into 3D garments. Unlike earlier tools that sculpted wrinkles and folds piece by piece—a time-consuming and expert-driven process—Marvelous Designer uses physics-based cloth simulation, allowing fast, accurate, and realistic draping of garments. This technology enables designers to visualize garments digitally before physical production, drastically reducing time and resource waste. --- ## Marvelous Designer’s Impact on the Film Industry This section details how Marvelous Designer revolutionized costume design in filmmaking with accurate, efficient garment visualization. Marvelous Designer has been widely adopted by the film industry for creating digital costumes in major productions such as *Black Panther*, *Avatar*, and *Guardians of the Galaxy*. The software supports pre-visualization processes, allowing costume designers to create 3D versions of garments to visualize how costumes look on characters before physical fabrication or filming. This is especially important in scenes involving CGI, fantasy storytelling, or dangerous stunts where real costumes may be impractical. The software’s simulation technology replaced the laborious sculpting of digital garments, providing realistic folds, wrinkles, and movement, thus enhancing the visual effects quality and efficiency. --- ## Use of CLO Software in Fashion Industry and Sustainability Benefits This section explores how CLO software supports fashion brands like H&M and Louis Vuitton by enabling 3D sample creation, reducing fabric waste, and promoting sustainability. Fashion brands utilize CLO’s software to replace multiple physical samples with 3D digital prototypes. This shift significantly reduces fabric consumption and waste, contributing positively to environmental sustainability. High-end brands like Louis Vuitton require extremely high-quality 3D samples that faithfully replicate real garments, including detailed components such as buttons, zippers, stitches, and trims. CLO’s software offers over 800 functions to refine these details in real-time, enabling designers to work as precisely as with physical garments. Additionally, the fashion industry leverages 3D content for communication with suppliers, virtual fashion shows, virtual showrooms, and virtual try-ons, further reducing carbon emissions by minimizing physical shipments and travel. --- ## Origins and Development of CLO and Marvelous Designer This section covers Jaden Oh’s background, the origins of CLO, and the evolution of Marvelous Designer from a niche tool for virtual cosplay to a mainstream software for fashion and film professionals. Jaden Oh, a computer scientist with a family background in clothing retail, began research on real-time cloth simulation over 20 years ago. His master's thesis included developing applications for online clothing simulation, which later evolved into Marvelous Designer. Initially, the software attracted a community of virtual cosplay enthusiasts who created digital costumes and tutorials, helping spread international recognition. This community-driven growth led to adoption by major VFX studios such as Weta Digital. The transition from sculpting-based tools to simulation-based software marked a paradigm shift, enabling rapid and realistic garment modeling. --- ## Technical Features and Challenges in Achieving Realism This section outlines the technical complexity behind CLO’s cloth simulation and the ongoing challenges in achieving lifelike garment quality. The software models garments as assemblies of 2D patterns sewn together, simulating fabric behavior through physics-based algorithms. Achieving the precise wrinkle formation, drape, and interaction requires extensive computation and advanced simulation techniques. Over a decade of development has resulted in more than 800 features supporting detailed components like buttons, zippers, stitches, and accessory trims. Despite these advances, challenges remain in balancing realism with usability and computational efficiency. --- ## Introduction of Genie: Democratizing 3D Garment Creation This section introduces Genie, CLO’s new software designed for non-experts to create 3D garments without pattern-making knowledge. While Marvelous Designer and CLO cater to professionals with expertise in garment patterns, Genie targets casual users and beginners by simplifying the garment design process. Genie allows users to create 3D clothing more easily, although some knowledge is still needed to produce real-life garments. The software carries full pattern and sewing information enabling 3D garments to be manufactured physically. This bridges the gap between digital design and real-world production. --- ## Personal Motivation and Vision Behind CLO This section shares Jaden Oh’s personal story and motivation for creating accessible garment design tools. Jaden’s motivation includes a personal story about his son attempting to create a garment using their software but failing due to complex patterns. This inspired the development of Genie to empower non-professionals, including children, to design and produce real garments. He emphasizes that his goal is to create software that his children and others can use to realize their creative ideas in fashion. --- ## Future Vision: CLOSET Platform and Industry Transformation This section discusses CLO’s future direction with the CLOSET platform aimed at revolutionizing the entire fashion lifecycle. Jaden envisions CLOSET as a collaborative platform where 3D garment data—rich with information like fabric consumption, sewing instructions, and supplier details—can be shared and accessed by multiple stakeholders in the fashion industry. The platform supports tech pack generation, virtual showrooms, and virtual try-ons, streamlining processes from design and production to retail and e-commerce. CLOSET is already in use by several major fashion companies, signaling a shift toward a fully digital, sustainable fashion ecosystem. --- ## Summary of Sustainability Impact and Industry Adoption - CLO software reduces physical sample production, minimizing fabric waste. - 3D digital samples enable virtual communication with suppliers, reducing carbon footprint. - Virtual fashion shows and try-ons further decrease environmental impact. - Major brands like Louis Vuitton, H&M, and film studios rely on CLO and Marvelous Designer. - CLO’s evolving tools address both expert professionals and casual users with Genie. --- # Key Terms and Brands - **CLO Virtual Fashion**: Company specializing in virtual garment software. - **Marvelous Designer (MD)**: Flagship 3D garment simulation software. - **Genie**: New, user-friendly 3D garment creation software. - **CLOSET**: Fashion collaboration platform for 3D garment data. - **Physics-based cloth simulation**: Technique modeling fabric behavior realistically. - **Virtual cosplay**: Digital costume play community. - **Sci-Tech Oscar**: Award from the U.S. Academy recognizing technical contributions to film. - **Weta Digital**: Renowned visual effects studio. - **Louis Vuitton, H&M**: Leading fashion brands using CLO software. - **Virtual try-ons, virtual showrooms**: Applications of 3D garment data in retail. --- This document consolidates the essential information from the interview to support semantic search and retrieval in fashion technology, digital garment simulation, and sustainable fashion innovation.
